ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a schematic diagram of an insect life cycle. In the lower left there is a row of egg-shaped structures labeled A, at the top there is a slender larva-like stage labeled B, on the right there is a curled transitional form labeled E, at the bottom there is an adult form labeled C/F, and arrows connect the stages to form a cycle. Reasoning: The question describes the stage in which “the larva undergoes a complete transformation inside a protective cocoon or hardened outer shell.” In complete metamorphosis, after the larva it enters the pupal stage, and the pupal stage is the stage of transforming into an adult. Therefore this part is the pupa, corresponding in the figure to the curled transitional form on the right.
